paper.title_en: Drift chambers consisting of mylar tubes with 0.125 mm wall thickness
paper.abstract_en: NRC “Kurchatov institute”– IHEP has mastered the technology of producing track chambers composed of 30 mm and 15 mm diameter drift tubes housed inside a pipe made of 0.125 mm thick mylar film coated with aluminum on both sides. The special ultrasonic welding stand has been constructed to produce a pipe with a longitudinal lap seam. The pipe made in this way is airtight, has a regular circular cross-section, straightness and rigidity, therefore the drift tube housed in it is, like traditional drift tube housed in a metallic tube, a self-supporting element capable to withstand the 350 g tension of the signal wire without additional supports and internal overpressure. This makes them convenient to manipulate when assembled into a chamber. Chambers consisting of three drift tube layers having tubes up to 2.5 m long have been manufactured and are successfully used in experiments at the 70-GeV proton synchrotron. Some technical and physical characteristics of the chambers of this design are presented.
